habitat: Pairs and loose flocks in dry thornveld, usually near the trees that hold their nests. They build nests at all times of year. The sexes are alike.
summary: A common resident. Dark brown above, with white eyebrows, white wing-bars and white feather edges. The underparts are white, and the bill is black. The legs are pink. In flight the rump and upper tail coverts are white. The immature has a horn-coloured bill. The call is a harsh chick-chick, and the song is loud and rambling. Avibase marks it rare or accidental in Kruger, so the months are unset. The Kemp paper name Whitebrowed Sparrowweaver and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Scaly-feathered Weaver is smaller, with a pink bill and a scaled forehead. White-browed Sparrow-Weaver has a black bill and a white eyebrow.

The Kemp code NB was left unchanged. No flight photograph was found. The grade A call is from Gauteng. Population figures and the Kemp name Whitebrowed Sparrowweaver were left unchanged.
